headline: 114 of 115 charges: Man City found guilty of financial breaches
summary: The Premier League giant faces potential points deductions or expulsion after an independent hearing found them guilty of nearly all financial regulation charges.
details: Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 out of 115 Premier League charges for breaching financial regulations, according to a report by The Athletic.
The club was accused of failing to provide accurate financial information and details of payments to players and coaches between 2009 and 2018.
Reports suggest the club inflated sponsorship revenue from Abu Dhabi state-controlled firms by disguising direct investments as income.
Other allegations included off-the-books payments to former manager Roberto Mancini via consultancy fees from a club in Abu Dhabi.
While no sanctions have been decided yet, City are expected to appeal the findings of the independent hearing.
Potential penalties could be severe, including a heavy points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.
Such a verdict could cast a shadow over City's eight Premier League titles and one Champions League trophy won in the last 15 years.
Other clubs may also seek to have City's titles stripped or claim compensation if it is proven they gained an unfair advantage.
caption:
114 out of 115 charges. Manchester City's trophy-laden era is now under threat.

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 out of 115 Premier League charges for breaching financial regulations, according to a report by The Athletic.

The club was accused of failing to provide accurate financial information and details of payments to players and coaches between 2009 and 2018.

Reports suggest the club inflated sponsorship revenue from Abu Dhabi state-controlled firms by disguising direct investments as income.

Other allegations included off-the-books payments to former manager Roberto Mancini via consultancy fees from a club in Abu Dhabi.

While no sanctions have been decided yet, City are expected to appeal the findings of the independent hearing.

Potential penalties could be severe, including a heavy points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.

Such a verdict could cast a shadow over City's eight Premier League titles and one Champions League trophy won in the last 15 years.

Other clubs may also seek to have City's titles stripped or claim compensation if it is proven they gained an unfair advantage.

headline_marked: Fuel price hike: [[Essential commodity prices soar]] in Bangladesh
headline: Fuel price hike: Essential commodity prices soar in Bangladesh
summary: Flour, rice, eggs, and vegetables are becoming costlier as traders cite higher transportation and production costs following a Tk 20-per-litre fuel increase.
details: The prices of several essential commodities have started rising again following a Tk 20-per-litre hike in fuel prices. Items including flour, rice, eggs, milk, cooking oil, lentils, and vegetables have all seen price increases.

Visits to Mohammadpur Krishi market, Town Hall market, and Karwan Bazar showed a trend of rising prices. For example, packaged flour rose to Tk 80 per kg last week and increased by another Tk 5 after the fuel hike.
A dozen eggs now cost Tk 160, while red lentils have risen to Tk 100 from Tk 90-95 per kg. Additionally, packaged liquid milk has become Tk 10 more expensive per litre.

Green chilli prices have almost doubled over the week, rising from Tk 80-100 to Tk 160-180 per kg. Round eggplants now cost Tk 140-160 per kg, while other vegetables like ridge gourd and snake gourd sell for Tk 80.

Traders attribute the increases to higher transportation and production costs. A rice shop shareholder in Mohammadpur noted that transport costs for bringing rice from Kushtia had risen by nearly Tk 5,000.

The government has raised the prices of diesel to Tk 135, kerosene to Tk 155, octane to Tk 165, and petrol to Tk 1 и 160 per litre. Consumers, however, allege that traders are using the fuel hike as a pretext to raise prices.

The Bangladesh Milk Producers' Cooperative Union (Milk Vita) attributed the increase in milk prices to higher gas, electricity, cattle feed, processing, and transportation costs, as well as frequent power outages.
